review_policy: Annual review and immediate review after a material concern or broken-link report.

organizations.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America
organizations.mission: Supports local clubs that provide young people with safe places, caring adults, and development opportunities.
organizations.alignment: Its emphasis on belonging, dependable relationships, and practical community presence reflects the movement’s welcome-first posture.
organizations.benefits: Young people, families, prospective volunteers, and local communities.

organizations.name: Save the Children US
organizations.mission: Works to improve children’s health, education, protection, and emergency support in the United States and around the world.
organizations.alignment: It connects practical service with the dignity and well-being of children and families.
organizations.benefits: Children and families affected by poverty, crisis, or limited access to essential support.

organizations.name: AdoptUSKids
organizations.mission: A federally funded national project that educates families about foster care and adoption and connects them with responsible state, territorial, and tribal systems.
organizations.alignment: It offers a credible first step without implying that Leave One Light On licenses homes or places children.
organizations.benefits: People exploring foster parenting or adoption from foster care, and child-welfare professionals.

organizations.name: National Foster Parent Association
organizations.mission: Provides education, advocacy resources, and support for foster, kinship, and adoptive families.
organizations.alignment: It recognizes that families need preparation, connection, and continuing support—not only recruitment.
organizations.benefits: Foster, kinship, and adoptive parents and the professionals who support them.

organizations.name: Dave Thomas Foundation for Adoption
organizations.mission: Works to increase adoptions from North America’s foster-care systems, including through its Wendy’s Wonderful Kids program.
organizations.alignment: Its focus on permanency for children waiting in foster care aligns with the movement’s concern for belonging and committed adults.
organizations.benefits: Children waiting in foster care, prospective adoptive families, and child-welfare systems.

organizations.name: MENTOR — Mentoring Connector
organizations.mission: Maintains a national database that helps people find youth-mentoring programs by location, youth served, and program type.
organizations.alignment: It helps visitors move from interest to a screened local program rather than attempting informal, unsupported contact.
organizations.benefits: Prospective mentors, families seeking programs, and mentoring organizations.

organizations.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America
organizations.mission: Creates and supports one-to-one mentoring relationships between caring adults and young people through local agencies.
organizations.alignment: Its focus on consistent, supported relationships reflects the movement’s belief in showing up over time.
organizations.benefits: Young people, parents or guardians, and adults considering a structured mentoring commitment.

organizations.name: Gary Sinise Foundation
organizations.mission: Serves veterans, first responders, their families, and those who have sacrificed through housing, wellness, outreach, and community programs.
organizations.alignment: It demonstrates gratitude through tangible service and long-term care for people who serve others.
organizations.benefits: Veterans, service members, first responders, and their families.

organizations.name: The Mission Continues
organizations.mission: Engages veterans in community-service projects and leadership opportunities after military service.
organizations.alignment: It connects continued purpose with practical service in local communities.
organizations.benefits: Veterans seeking service and connection, and communities seeking volunteer leadership.

organizations.name: American Red Cross Blood Services
organizations.mission: Collects blood, platelets, and plasma and helps eligible donors find appointments and understand donation requirements.
organizations.alignment: Blood donation is a direct, often anonymous act of practical compassion.
organizations.benefits: Eligible blood donors, blood-drive hosts, volunteers, and patients who rely on blood products.

organizations.name: America’s Blood Centers
organizations.mission: Represents independent community blood centers and helps people locate blood-donation organizations.
organizations.alignment: It broadens the path beyond any single collection organization and supports locally supplied blood care.
organizations.benefits: Eligible donors, community blood centers, hospitals, and patients.

organizations.name: NMDP
organizations.mission: Connects patients with blood stem-cell donors and supports cellular therapy, research, and patient services.
organizations.alignment: It offers another deeply personal way eligible people may help someone they may never meet.
organizations.benefits: Patients needing blood stem-cell therapy, potential registry members, donors, and families.

organizations.name: Points of Light
organizations.mission: Connects people and organizations with volunteer opportunities, civic-service resources, and local networks.
organizations.alignment: It helps visitors find practical ways to serve according to their time, abilities, and community.
organizations.benefits: Individuals, families, companies, nonprofits, and community volunteer leaders.

organizations.name: AmeriCorps
organizations.mission: A federal agency supporting national service and volunteer programs addressing community needs across the United States.
organizations.alignment: It offers structured service pathways for people ready for a deeper time commitment.
organizations.benefits: People considering national service, community organizations, and volunteers seeking structured opportunities.

organizations.name: Feeding America
organizations.mission: Supports a nationwide network of food banks and helps visitors find food assistance or local volunteer opportunities.
organizations.alignment: It connects immediate human need with concrete local action and respect for neighbors.
organizations.benefits: People seeking food assistance, volunteers, food banks, and community partners.

organizations.name: Meals on Wheels America
organizations.mission: Supports local programs delivering meals, connection, and safety checks to older adults.
organizations.alignment: A meal and a human visit are practical expressions of care, dignity, and dependable presence.
organizations.benefits: Older adults, caregivers, local volunteers, and community meal programs.

organizations.name: Direct Relief
organizations.mission: Provides medical aid and emergency health support in response to disasters, poverty, and other urgent needs.
organizations.alignment: It emphasizes practical, professionally coordinated assistance where health systems and communities are under strain.
organizations.benefits: Health facilities, communities affected by disasters, and people seeking responsible ways to support relief.

organizations.name: Team Rubicon
organizations.mission: Mobilizes veteran-led volunteer teams to help communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.
organizations.alignment: It combines continued service, practical skill, and disciplined disaster response.
organizations.benefits: Disaster-affected communities, veterans, first responders, and qualified volunteers.

organizations.name: Habitat for Humanity
organizations.mission: Works with local communities and families to build, repair, and improve homes and offers local volunteer opportunities.
organizations.alignment: Safe, stable housing and neighbors working beside one another reflect practical hospitality.
organizations.benefits: Families seeking housing pathways, homeowners needing repairs, and local volunteers.

organizations.name: National Alliance to End Homelessness
organizations.mission: Uses research, education, and policy analysis to support effective responses to homelessness.
organizations.alignment: It helps visitors understand housing instability through evidence rather than stereotypes or outrage.
organizations.benefits: Service providers, researchers, community leaders, and people learning about homelessness solutions.

organizations.mission: Connects people with local health and human-service information through regional 211 networks.
organizations.alignment: It gives visitors a practical place to begin when a need is local and the appropriate provider is unclear.
organizations.benefits: People seeking local assistance, caregivers, families, and community members.

organizations.name: VolunteerMatch
organizations.mission: Helps people search for volunteer opportunities offered by participating organizations.
organizations.alignment: It allows guests to choose service that fits their location, interests, skills, and availability.
organizations.benefits: Prospective volunteers and organizations recruiting volunteers.
